policy: Sourced historical political context, independently reviewed from period institutions and governing doctrines. This supplement is unscored and does not replace, filter or alter equal-axis closest-ideology comparisons. Regimes can contain competing traditions; these descriptions do not classify all citizens.

entries.label: Settler nationalism and minority rule
entries.rationale: The Rhodesian Front defended white-minority political control and settler sovereignty through racially restricted parliamentary institutions. Authoritarian capitalism is a broad economic comparison, not the complete historical tradition.

sources.title: Possible Speeding up of Southern Rhodesian UDI
Land Inequality and Income Distribution in Rhodesia

entries.label: Imperialism and colonial rule
entries.rationale: Interwar parliamentary government in Britain coexisted with colonial administration, racial inequality and growing dominion autonomy. Militarism describes one policy dimension rather than the empire’s whole political tradition.

sources.title: Colonial Office records and colonial administration
Britain’s Empire Marketing Board and the failure of soft trade policy, 1926–33

entries.label: Nazism
entries.rationale: National Socialism was the governing party ideology: racial hierarchy, antisemitism, dictatorship and expansionism. This classification is directly historical, distinct from a numerical resemblance.

entries.label: Marxism–Leninism under Stalin
entries.rationale: The selected 1928–1953 period concerns Stalinist party rule, central planning and the official Marxist–Leninist doctrine. Communism is a broader family label, not a substitute for this period-specific description.

sources.title: Internal Workings of the Soviet Union
Constitution of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics

entries.label: Tsarist monarchism
entries.rationale: After 1906 the Fundamental Laws combined a legislature with extensive imperial executive powers and Orthodox establishment. The state contained competing movements; nationalist conservatism alone does not describe its dynastic institutions.

sources.publisher: Northern Virginia Community College (Russian primary text)
sources.title: 1906 Fundamental Laws

entries.label: Patrician republicanism
entries.rationale: Late Venice was an oligarchic republic governed by a hereditary patriciate, with merchant interests and a restricted political community. Traditional conservatism is a modern comparison, not an official Venetian party doctrine.

sources.title: Reform, Revolution, and the End of the Republic

entries.label: Tanzimat reform and dynastic rule
entries.rationale: The 1839–1876 reform period pursued administrative centralisation, new civil institutions and qualified equality while retaining the sultanate and Islamic institutions. A capitalist-authoritarian label omits these dynastic and reforming foundations.

sources.publisher: Cambridge University Press (Joel Beinin; hosted by Cankaya University)
sources.title: Ottoman reform and European imperialism, 1839–1907

entries.label: Habsburg dynastic constitutionalism
entries.rationale: The dual monarchy combined hereditary imperial authority with separate Austrian and Hungarian constitutional institutions and competing national movements. It did not have one uniform nationalist party ideology.

sources.title: Austro-Hungarian Relations 1867–1914: A Community of Conflict

entries.label: Imperial monarchism and conservatism
entries.rationale: The Kaiser appointed the government within a federal constitutional monarchy containing several political parties. Conservative imperial institutions and nationalism were important, without making every citizen or parliamentary party conservative.

entries.label: Emperor-centred ultranationalism
entries.rationale: During 1931–1945 military influence, imperial expansion and kokutai doctrine centred the emperor and Japanese national polity. The regime was not Nazi Germany; its relationship to the wider category of fascism is debated.

sources.title: Japan: Key points in modern history
The Japanese Economy during the Interwar Period

entries.label: Confucian dynastic rule and late-Qing reform
entries.rationale: The late Qing retained imperial and Confucian legitimacy while adopting selective military, industrial and constitutional reforms. Traditional conservatism is an analogy rather than a historically named governing party ideology.

sources.title: The Qing State’s Influence on Early Manufacturing of the 1910s

entries.label: Oligarchic republicanism
entries.rationale: Merchant regents, provincial institutions and the House of Orange competed within a confederated republic. Neoconservatism is a twentieth-century movement and is anachronistic as the republic’s classification.

sources.title: Trouble in paradise: The Dutch golden age

entries.label: Napoleonic imperial rule
entries.rationale: Napoleon’s hereditary imperial regime combined personal authority, plebiscitary legitimacy, civil law and revolutionary legacies. Bonapartism describes this political tradition and its later development; fascism emerged more than a century afterward.

sources.title: Was the Napoleonic regime a military dictatorship?
Le Code Civil: naissance, principes et posterite

entries.label: Parliamentary democratic republicanism
entries.rationale: The republic’s constitutional framework allowed competitive parties, adult suffrage and parliamentary government. Presidential emergency government increasingly weakened it after 1930. Communitarianism is a numerical comparison, not the republic’s governing doctrine.

entries.label: Fascism
entries.rationale: Mussolini’s National Fascist Party governed through dictatorship, corporatism and nationalist mobilisation while retaining the monarchy until 1943. Fascism is the period’s actual party ideology.

sources.publisher: Internet Modern History Sourcebook / Fordham University
sources.title: Mussolini: The Doctrine of Fascism

entries.label: Francoism and National Catholicism
entries.rationale: Early Francoism joined military dictatorship, Catholic traditionalism, nationalism and Falangist elements. Its fascist components do not erase monarchist, clerical and military traditions or make the whole selected period identical to Italian fascism.

entries.label: Authoritarian Catholic corporatism
entries.rationale: Salazar’s Estado Novo combined corporatism, conservative Catholic alignment, dictatorship and colonial nationalism. Fascist influence and parallels require qualification; its classification as fascism is disputed.

sources.title: O Estado Novo: Constituicao e reformas da Administracao

entries.label: Marxism–Leninism
entries.rationale: The SED’s official Marxist–Leninist doctrine and Soviet-aligned party state governed during the Honecker period. Maoism is a distinct Chinese revolutionary tradition and is not the GDR’s state ideology.

entries.label: Titoism and self-management socialism
entries.rationale: Tito’s Yugoslavia combined communist party leadership, social ownership, worker self-management, federal decentralisation and nonalignment. Cuban Socialism is a different national tradition, despite overlapping axis scores.

sources.publisher: Coordinamento Nazionale per la Jugoslavia (Yugoslav primary text)
sources.title: Constitution of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia

entries.label: Parliamentary democratic republicanism
entries.rationale: The 1920 constitution established a democratic republic with competitive parties, rights and parliamentary institutions. The framework contained several ideologies; communitarianism was not a single official state doctrine.
